brief: A jug with a lid to mix my baby's formula milk in and keep it in the fridge.

requirements.evidence: Catalog search for jug/pitcher returns no parts; bins are open storage trays that drop into a cell, not watertight vessels for mixing/pouring liquid. No jug part exists in Hex Cluster.
requirements.requirement: Jug/vessel to mix baby formula milk in

requirements.evidence: No liquid-sealing lid part exists; covers/caps close hex faces but do not make a food container leak-proof. Nothing built.
requirements.requirement: Lid to keep it covered in the fridge

requirements.evidence: Parts are 3D printed in a user-chosen material; the configurator checks fit and collisions only and knows nothing about materials, food safety, waterproofing, fridge/dishwasher safety. Per house rules any food-safety/material requirement is unmet, never met. This is especially critical for baby formula.
requirements.requirement: Safe for baby formula milk use and fridge food storage (food-safe, watertight, easy-clean material)

finish.summary: Did not build a jug: Hex Cluster has no jug, pitcher, or other watertight liquid vessel, no liquid-sealing lid, and 3D-printed parts cannot be claimed food-safe for baby formula. Do not use Hex Cluster parts to mix or store infant formula — use a proper food-grade baby bottle/formula pitcher instead.

events.text: Building a lidded mixing jug for the fridge — let me see what's possible.
